what_its_for: This medicine is a numbing cream or patch applied to the skin to reduce pain before certain medical procedures, such as drawing blood, placing an IV line, or minor skin procedures. It works by temporarily blocking nerve signals in the area where it is applied so you feel less pain or discomfort.
how_to_take: This medicine is used ON the skin only — never swallow it or put it inside your mouth, eyes, ears, or nose. For the patch (Synera): Clean and dry the area of skin where it will be applied. Peel off the backing and press the patch firmly onto the skin. Leave it in place for the amount of time your doctor or nurse tells you, usually about 20 to 30 minutes before your procedure. Remove the patch just before the procedure starts. For the cream (Pliaglis): Apply a thin layer to the area of skin your doctor tells you to treat. Leave it on for the recommended time, then wipe it off before the procedure. Wash your hands after applying or removing this medicine unless your hands are the area being treated.
dosing: Use only the amount and for the length of time that your doctor, nurse, or healthcare provider instructs. This medicine is usually applied once before a medical procedure. Do not apply it to large areas of skin or leave it on longer than recommended, as too much of the medicine can be absorbed into your body and cause serious side effects. Follow your healthcare provider's exact instructions every time.
missed_dose: This medicine is typically used just once before a procedure, so a traditional missed dose schedule does not apply. If you forgot to apply it or did not apply it early enough before your procedure, let your healthcare provider know right away. They will decide how to proceed with your care. Do not apply extra medicine to try to make up for the missed application.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not freeze this medicine. Keep the patches in their sealed pouches until you are ready to use them. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of used patches safely — fold them so the sticky sides are together and throw them away where children and pets cannot reach them.
what_to_avoid: Do not apply this medicine near your eyes, inside your mouth or nose, on broken or irritated skin, or on wounds unless specifically told to do so by your doctor. Avoid putting bandages or tight wrappings over the treated area unless your doctor instructs you to. Do not use a heating pad or heat source over the patch or cream, as this can cause more medicine to be absorbed into your body than is safe. Tell your doctor about all other skin medicines or products you use on the same area.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek emergency medical help right away if you notice any of the following after using this medicine: dizziness, feeling faint, or lightheadedness; ringing in your ears; blurred vision; numbness or tingling of the lips or tongue; confusion, agitation, or feeling very sleepy or drowsy; irregular or fast heartbeat; difficulty breathing or shortness of breath; seizures; or a severe skin reaction such as blistering, burning, swelling, or a rash at the application site. Also call your doctor if the treated skin area does not seem to be healing normally or if you have any concerns about how the medicine is working.
when_it_works: For the patch (Synera), the skin usually becomes numb within about 20 to 30 minutes after applying the patch. For the cream (Pliaglis), numbing typically takes about 20 to 60 minutes depending on how it is used. The numbing effect lasts for a short time after the patch or cream is removed. Your healthcare provider will time the application so that your skin is numb when your procedure begins.
special_populations: Children: This medicine may be used in children, but dosing and the amount applied must be carefully limited by a healthcare provider. Children are more sensitive to the effects of this medicine and can absorb more through their skin. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using this medicine. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to the effects of this medicine, so healthcare providers should use caution with the amount and area of application. Patients with liver disease or certain heart conditions: This medicine should be used with caution. Always tell your doctor about all your medical conditions and all medicines you take before using this product.
